questions.q: What is a database index, in plain terms?
options: A separate structure the database maintains on specific fields that lets it find matching rows directly, instead of checking every row
A backup copy of the entire table
A list of every user who has ever viewed a record
A setting that deletes old records automatically
questions.explain: An index lets the database jump to matching rows directly, the way a book's index lets you jump to a page instead of reading the whole book.

questions.q: Without an index on the field being filtered, how does the database find matching rows?
options: It refuses to run the query
It checks every row in the table, one at a time, to see if it matches
It automatically builds a temporary index first
It only checks the first 100 rows
questions.explain: With no index to jump to matches directly, the only option left is checking each row in turn — a full table scan.

questions.q: What is the real cost of adding an index to a table?
options: Indexes slow down reads but speed up writes
Every insert or update to the table now also has to update that index, plus the index consumes additional storage
Indexes have no real cost once configured
Indexes only cost money if the table has fewer than 1,000 records
questions.explain: Indexes speed up reads but slow down writes, since the index itself must be kept accurate on every insert and update — and it takes extra storage too.

questions.q: Where is indexing configured on the ServiceNow platform?
options: In a single instance-wide toggle that indexes every table at once
At the field's Dictionary Entry, table by table and field by field
Only ServiceNow Support can configure indexes, never an admin
In the Slow Request Log settings
questions.explain: Indexing ties back to the table's own Dictionary — the same Dictionary Entries used to define a field's type and validation.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which fields are the right ones to consider indexing?
options: Every field on every table, to be safe
Fields that show up often in real filter conditions or sort orders, especially on large tables
Only fields that are never used in any query
Only fields with the word "date" in the name
questions.explain: Indexing fields actually used in Encoded Query conditions and sort orders captures the read benefit; indexing unused fields only adds write cost.
